title: Giraffe Tongues Are Almost Black. Is 12 Hours of Sun Why? 🦒
description:
Why is a giraffe's tongue dark purple, almost black? A giraffe's 45-50 cm tongue spends hours a day out in the African sun, and scientists think the dark pigment at the front works like built-in sunscreen, though the okapi's identical forest tongue keeps it a mystery.

Sources:
https://giraffeconservation.org/facts-about-giraffe/how-long-is-a-giraffes-tongue-what-color-is-it/
https://www.iflscience.com/why-do-giraffes-have-dark-purple-tongues-83408

Animated in the Kawaii Anime style.

topic: Why is a giraffe's tongue dark purple?
script:
Giraffe tongues are almost black,
and you'd never guess why.
They can spend up to twelve hours a day out in the sun.
That tongue is forty-five to fifty centimeters long,
longer than your whole forearm.
It wraps thorny acacia branches like a hand,
and tough little bumps called papillae
armor it against the spikes.
But all that eating happens in the African sun.
So scientists think the dark color is built-in sunscreen.
The front, the part that sticks out,
is packed with dark pigment.
The base, tucked inside the mouth,
is plain pink.
And honestly, that's kind of genius.
But it's not proven.
The okapi, the giraffe's forest cousin,
has the same dark tongue in the shade.
So why is a giraffe's tongue almost black?
Sunscreen, or something else?
key_facts: Giraffe tongues are about 45-50 cm (17-19 in) long (Giraffe Conservation Foundation; IFLScience)
The front of the tongue is dark blue-black-purple; the base, kept inside the mouth, is pink (GCF)
Leading theory: the dark pigment protects the exposed tongue from sunburn while feeding; not fully accepted (GCF; IFLScience 'much debate')
Giraffes can spend up to about 12 hours a day feeding (IFLScience; GCF gives a higher figure)
Thickened papillae armor the prehensile tongue against acacia thorns (GCF; IFLScience)
The okapi, the giraffe's closest relative, has a similar dark tongue in the rainforest (GCF)
